text:
Stephen Kinnock has been promoted to cabinet by the new prime minister

Former Labour leader Lord Neil Kinnock has described news of his son's appointment as Welsh secretary as "a delight".

Stephen Kinnock was given his first cabinet role after Andy Burnham took over as prime minister on Monday.

The Aberafan Maesteg MP, who had been a health minister, replaces Cardiff East MP Jo Stevens.

Lord Kinnock, 84, said his son had earned the promotion through "a lifetime of action and service" and would be able to advance Welsh interests at the heart of government.

Stephen Kinnock described the appointment as the "privilege of my life".

Stephen Kinnock with his parents, Neil and the late Glenys, and his sister, Rachel in 1992

Speaking to BBC Radio Wales Breakfast Lord Kinnock, Labour's leader from 1983 to 1992, said he had spoken to his son late on Monday night.

"He was thrilled to bits," Lord Kinnock said.

"We had our midnight conversation, not the first in our lives it has to be said, and usually that was because he came home late.

"It was a delight."

"Now as secretary of state he'll be in a position to directly influence UK affairs in a way that benefits our country," he added.

Stephen Kinnock pledged to champion Wales within government.

He said he would work across governments to deliver for Welsh communities and build "a strong Wales within a strong United Kingdom".

Jo Stevens had faced criticism from some Welsh Labour politicians for not supporting more powers for the Welsh government, such as for policing, with one former minister describing her as "anti-devolution".

But she said Wales saw its biggest budget settlement for public services in the history of devolution while she was in office.

Stevens added: "Wales has seen the biggest budget settlement for our public services in the history of devolution, our steel industry saved and transformed for the future, the largest public investment in Wales in history through new nuclear at Wylfa, a generational commitment of Â£14bn for our Welsh railways, the best local growth fund settlement of any of the UK nations and so much more.

"I wish the new prime minister and my successor the very best in their new roles and know that they will do a great job, alongside our new Welsh Labour leader Ken Skates, in delivering for the people of Wales."

Stevens said it had been "a privilege and an honour" for her to have been Welsh secretary since Labour returned to power at Westminster in 2024.

Jo Stevens is leaving the post of Welsh secretary, which was was created in the 1960s

Wales' first minister urged the new prime minister to "turn his commitment to devolution into action" and said he hoped to build a "positive and productive relationship" with the new UK government.

In his first call with Andy Burnham, Rhun ap Iorwerth called for Wales to gain control of policing, justice, rail and the Crown Estate.

Downing Street said the prime minister had spoken to the leaders of Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland and wanted a "collaborative, practical and pragmatic" relationship with the devolved administrations.

A spokesperson said closer working could help deliver "deeper devolution" and boost economic growth.

Plaid Cymru's Westminster leader Liz Saville Roberts congratulated Stephen Kinnock on his appointment, despite describing the Welsh secretary role as an "anachronism" that sits uneasily with devolution.

She said Plaid hoped to build a constructive relationship with Kinnock and looked forward to discussions about devolving rail infrastructure, the Crown Estate, justice and policing, adding that the party's Senedd election victory in May gave it a "clear mandate" that should be respected.

Burnham gave his first speech as prime minister outside Number 10 on Monday

Speaking to BBC Radio Wales Breakfast, Tonia Antoniazzi said it had been a "brutal 24 hours" for colleagues and friends.

The Member of Parliament for Gower added that Burnham and Kinnock had to turn the tide following Labour's historic defeat in Senedd in May.

"I think people saw Reform as either being a protest vote. A lot of our voters went to vote Reform or Plaid Cymru, and there has been a change in the Senedd and we accept that," she said.

Antoniazzi, who is also the chair of the Northern Ireland Committee, said she was looking forward to working with Chris Bryant, MP for Rhondda and Ogmore, who had been promoted to the role of Secretary of State for Northern Ireland.

The son of former Labour leader Neil Kinnock and former MEP Glenys Kinnock, he was born in Tredegar, Blaenau Gwent.

He has two children with the former Danish prime minister Helle Thorning-Schmidt.

Kinnock was elected to serve Aberavon in the 2015 general election.

Keir Starmer appointed him as a junior health minister for England when Labour came to power at Westminster in 2024 with Kinnock representing the newly named constituency of Aberafan Maesteg.

Torfaen MP Nick Thomas-Symonds is also leaving government

Vale of Glamorgan MP Kanishka Narayan will be the minister for artificial intelligence and will also attend cabinet.

Meanwhile, Torfaen MP and Starmer loyalist Nick Thomas-Symonds announced he would be leaving government after holding a key role as the UK's chief negotiator with the European Union.

In a letter on X, he said it had been "an honour to have a role at the centre of government" and he was leaving office with the UK-EU relationship in a "far better state than when I took up the role in July 2024".
